text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:

- Slovenia's economic and social board discussed the state of the economy and economic plans to the year 2001 on Wednesday. It said talks between employers, government and unions on workers' social benefits will continue next week.
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said he expected parliamentary parties to reach agreement this week on bringing Slovenia's constitution in line with EU norms.
- President Milan Kucan met U.S. ambassador Victor Jackovich on Wednesday to discuss Slovenia's failure to qualify for the first round of NATO expansion.
- Some 12 percent of all privatisation vouchers that expire at the end of this month, have not yet been spent, the ministry of economic relations and development said.
- Rescue teams are still searching for a police diver who died during a routine exercise in an underground lake on Tuesday.

- Slovenian investment funds said they could be listed on Ljubljana bourse as early as September if parliament passes the law next month offering additional state capital in exchange for privatisation vouchers.
- A Slovenian Bishops' Conference said on Wednesday it was ready to take up an invitation by Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek to start talks with Slovenian state representatives.
